diagnostic_evidence.quote: There exist a compact set $\mathcal{K}\subset \mathbb{C}^d$, with $\mathcal{U} \subset \mathcal{K}$

Moreover, assume that the compact set $\mathcal{K}\subseteq\C^d $ of assumption  \ref{ass:diffusion_matrix} is such that $\mathcal{E}_{\bm{\rho}}\subset\mathring{\mathcal{K}}$ for some $\bm{\rho}>\bm{1}$

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem demands a compact K ⊆ C^d with K ⊂ U = [-1,1]^d, while the invoked Assumption ass:diffusion_matrix requires U ⊂ K; jointly they force K = U, whose interior in C^d is empty, so both conclusions (holomorphic extension to the interior of K, and the uniform bound over compact subsets of that interior) are vacuous. Moreover, the corollaries apply the theorem with a Bernstein polyellipse E_ρ contained in the interior of K (ρ > 1 componentwise), and E_ρ contains non-real points, which is incompatible with K ⊂ U ⊂ R^d; as literally stated, thm:mainthm therefore cannot be invoked in their proofs. The proof itself only uses the Assumption's inclusion U ⊂ K and never uses K ⊂ U.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the hypothesis to the intended inclusion U ⊂ K, as in Assumption ass:diffusion_matrix (e.g., reverse or delete the clause 'K ⊂ U'); the proof and all three corollaries then apply unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the paper's main holomorphy theorem carries no content, and the derivations of Corollaries cor:maincor, cor:LS and cor:CS, each of which applies thm:mainthm with E_ρ contained in the interior of K, do not go through on the literal statement.
issues.title: Main theorem hypothesis reverses the inclusion (K subset of U), contradicting Assumption 3.5 and making the statement vacuous
issues.why_classification: A one-line, forced correction of the hypothesis (the only reading consistent with Assumption ass:diffusion_matrix and with the corollaries' hypotheses) requires no new argument and preserves the theorem and every downstream claim, rate, and guarantee.

issues.failure_explanation: The integral form of the ODE u̇(t) = M(t)u(t) is u(t) = u_0 + ∫_0^t M(s)u(s)ds, so the Volterra kernel must be h(t,s,u,z) = M̃(s,z)u. With h(t,s,u,z) = M̃(t,z)u as written, the displayed Volterra equation freezes the matrix at the outer time t instead of the integration variable s and is a different equation: e.g., for the scalar problem u̇ = t·u, u(0) = 1, the ODE gives e^{t^2/2} whereas the displayed equation gives a different function. Consequently Step 1 establishes existence, uniqueness and holomorphy for the wrong object (in general the constructed extension does not agree with f on U), and Step 2's starting point, that ũ satisfies u̇̃ = M̃ũ, does not follow from Step 1 as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace M̃(t,z) by M̃(s,z) in the definition of h, so that the Volterra equation is the integral form of the ODE; all subsequent verifications (continuity, holomorphy, Lipschitz bound) are unchanged, and Step 2 then applies to the object constructed in Step 1.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the main theorem does not, as written, construct the solution of the diffusion equation (eq:ted) or establish its holomorphic parameter dependence; the corollaries whose proofs invoke thm:mainthm inherit the gap.
issues.title: Volterra reformulation in the proof of the main theorem evaluates the kernel at t instead of the integration variable s
issues.why_classification: A single forced substitution repairs the construction; no hypothesis, conclusion, rate, or downstream claim changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for any $f: \mathcal{U} \rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ that admits a holomorphic extension to a Bernstein polyellipse $\mathcal{E}_{\bm{\rho}} \subset \mathbb{C}^d$

Let $0<\epsilon < 1$, $\varrho$ be either the uniform or Chebyschev measure on $\mathcal{U}=[-1,1]^d$, $m \geq 3$ and $\bm{y}_1, \dots , \bm{y}_m $ independent and identically distributed drawn from the probability distribution $ \varrho$.

issues.failure_explanation: The stated bound is homogeneous of degree zero in f, but the least-squares error scales linearly with f: replacing f by λf in th:main_ls (or scaling the initial condition u_0 by λ in cor:LS, which leaves every hypothesis intact, since Assumption ass:diffusion_matrix constrains only C) multiplies the error by λ while the right-hand side C(ρ,p)(m/log(m/ε))^{1/2−1/p} + 2‖n‖_∞ is unchanged, so the inequality fails for large λ. The magnitude factor ‖f‖_{L^∞(E_ρ)} (respectively B(u_0,T,M) of eq:bound_term, which the parallel compressed-sensing corollary cor:CS does include) is missing, so th:main_ls and cor:LS are false as stated; the argument via the cited theorem can only establish the bound with this factor. In addition, p appears in both bounds but is never quantified (a decaying rate requires p < 2), and in th:main_ls the quantifier order ('there exists a set S … for any f …') together with the unquantified ρ leaves the claim ill-defined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate th:main_ls and cor:LS with the multiplicative magnitude factor (‖f‖_{L^∞(E_ρ)} in th:main_ls; B(u_0,T,M) as defined in eq:bound_term in cor:LS, matching cor:CS) and add the missing quantification of p (e.g., 0 < p ≤ 1 as in cor:CS, or the range of the cited theorem); the convergence rate and all other guarantees are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The least-squares convergence guarantee (Theorem th:main_ls, Corollary cor:LS, and the corresponding unlabelled display in Section 2.4) is false/ill-posed as stated; the abstract's and introduction's claims of convergence guarantees for least-squares surrogates are supported only after the bound is restated with the magnitude factor and a quantified p.
issues.title: Least-squares convergence bounds omit the solution-magnitude factor and never quantify p
issues.why_classification: The stated guarantee of a central convergence theorem and its corollary is false (trivial scaling counterexample) and ill-posed (unquantified p); the repair is local but necessarily weakens the stated bound by restoring the norm dependence, a limited weakening that leaves a recognizably comparable result without new proof architecture.
